notes.content: The page names Multomb(F) the grande multiombre, or M-multiombre, and states that it is a set-theoretic figure in M, faithfully indexed by the deployment tilde F, whose knowledge determines F. It then uses L hooked into M and inverse images to obtain (1.9): F-family to P(L), F mapped to omb(F), and F-family to Fig(L), F mapped to multomb(F). The text explicitly declines to expect injectivity of the first map and gives only a tendency toward injectivity for the second. It names omb(F) the petite ombre, or ombre when confusion seems excluded, and multomb the (petite) multiombre.
math_reading_decisions: Capital Multomb in the first definition and lower-case omb/multomb in (1.9) and the final definitions are preserved.
The doubled F in the opening definition is transcribed literally as mathbb F. I did not silently replace it by the ordinary F one might expect from the sentence.

The P handwriting remains uncertain between calligraphic and script forms; H's fraktur rendering is not established. F as the domain family also remains uncertain between calligraphic and fraktur. Each recurring doubt is marked at its first page occurrence only.
The Fig inverse-image arrow has a single upper barb. Its application meaning does not justify adding an unseen lower barb.

Both arrows in (1.9) have cancelled hooks and live right-pointing shafts/heads. The accompanying injectivity discussion is compatible with this correction, but was not used as a substitute for reading the ink.
The t in multomb in (1.9)b is heavily retraced. The crop does not recover an additional old letter or a distinct cancellation; no deleted text was manufactured.
The foot barred m is a verbal abbreviation for même, not an equation sign. It remains abbreviated in the page.
No theorem is proved on this page. The assertions about faithful indexing, recovery of F and possible injectivity were read and internally parsed, not independently proved.
author_doubts: “dont la première n'a aucune raison d'être injective, la seconde par contre a une tendance à l'être” — the manuscript's qualified injectivity statement; a cross-shaped mark follows.
“quand une confusion semble exclue” — the author's qualification for using the shorter name ombre.
“Jusqu'à présent il n'était pas question de L.” — retrospective scope check in an insertion, not a question.
